name: Salesforce Certified Platform Developer (formerly Platform Developer I)
prereq: None. The Salesforce Certified Platform Administrator credential is recommended but not required.
delivery: Booked through Trailhead Academy and delivered by Pearson VUE, either online proctored or at a testing center. No hard-copy or online materials allowed during the exam.
maintenance: Complete the Platform Developer certification maintenance badge on Trailhead once a year (Winter '26 badge due December 4, 2026); the credential expires if you miss the deadline.

sections.title: Developer Fundamentals
objectives: Understand multi-tenant concepts and design frameworks, such as MVC architecture and Lightning Component Framework.
Given a scenario, identify common use cases and best practices for declarative versus programmatic customizations, including governor limits, formula fields, and roll-up summaries.
Given a scenario, determine, create, and access the appropriate data model including objects, fields, relationships, and external IDs.
Understand use cases and limitations of using Agentforce for Developers.

sections.title: Process Automation and Logic
objectives: Identify the capabilities of the declarative process automation features.
Understand how to declare variables, constants, methods, modifiers, Apex interfaces, and the appropriate use cases for each.
Given a scenario, assess how Apex control flow statements will execute and when to apply different control flow statements.
Given a scenario, write SOSL, SOQL, and DML statements in Apex, and assess what they will return.
Given a scenario, follow best practices to write Apex classes and triggers.
Given a scenario, understand governor limits and their implications on Apex transactions.
Describe the relationship between Apex transactions, the save order of execution, and the potential for recursion and/or cascading.
Implement exception handling in Apex, including custom exceptions as needed.
Given a scenario, use declarative functionality and Apex together to automate business logic.

sections.title: User Interface
objectives: Given a scenario, prevent user interface and data access security vulnerabilities.
Given a scenario, display and use custom user interface components, including Lightning components, Flow, and Visualforce.
Describe the use cases and best practices for Lightning Web Components, including the framework, benefits, and events.
Given a scenario, implement Apex to work with various types of page components, including Lightning components, Flow, and Agentforce.

sections.title: Testing, Debugging, and Deployment
objectives: Write and execute tests for triggers, controllers, classes, and flows using various sources of test data.
Given a scenario, know how and when to use the Salesforce Developer tools such as Salesforce DX, Salesforce CLI, and Developer Console.
Describe how to approach debugging system issues and monitoring flows, performance, asynchronous, and batch jobs.
Describe the environments, requirements, and process for deploying code and associated configurations.

tips: Read the official exam guide first and weight study time by section: Process Automation and Logic is 28% and Developer Fundamentals 27% of the exam.
Do the four official Cert Prep modules on Trailhead; each has practice questions and flashcards for its section.
Practice in a free Developer Edition org or Trailhead Playground; writing real Apex and LWC beats reading about it.
Expect short scenarios with code snippets; read the last line (what is being asked) before the code.
Multiple-select questions tell you how many answers to choose; all must be correct to score.
There is no penalty for guessing, so answer every question and flag uncertain ones for review.
Budget under 2 minutes per question (up to 65 questions in 105 minutes) and leave 10 minutes to revisit flagged items.
Up to 5 unscored questions are mixed in; don't let an odd question rattle you.
Know the core governor limits (100/200 SOQL queries, 150 DML statements, 50,000 rows) and the save order of execution cold; they recur across sections.
When a question asks for the best solution, check if a declarative tool (formula, roll-up summary, flow) solves it before choosing code.
Questions align to the Summer '25 release; newer default behaviors (such as user mode by default in API 67.0+) may not match the exam's answers.
For online proctoring, run the Pearson VUE system test in advance, clear your desk, and check in 20-30 minutes early with a valid government-issued ID.
Schedule the exam date first; a fixed deadline keeps a 4-6 week plan on track.

tasks: Read the official exam guide end to end
Complete Cert Prep: Developer Fundamentals
Complete Data Modeling; build a lookup and a master-detail with a roll-up summary
Complete Formulas and Validation; list what each declarative tool can and can't do
Try Agentforce for Developers in VS Code and note its limits
Complete Apex Basics & Database
Practice variables, constants, access modifiers, interfaces and control flow (if, for, switch)
Write SOQL (with relationship queries) and SOSL, and predict what each returns
Practice DML statements vs Database methods with allOrNone=false
Complete Apex Triggers; bulkify a trigger with one query and one DML outside loops
Study Triggers and Order of Execution; trace a save with a flow, a trigger and a workflow update
Write try/catch with a custom exception
Complete Record-Triggered Flows and call Apex from a flow with @InvocableMethod
Complete Lightning Web Components Basics
Call Apex from LWC with @wire (cacheable=true) and imperatively; show errors
Send data parent-to-child with @api and child-to-parent with CustomEvent
Complete Visualforce Basics: standard controller, custom controller and extension
Review XSS and SOQL injection prevention, sharing keywords and user mode
Complete Apex Testing; use @TestSetup, Test.startTest/stopTest and System.assert methods
Reach 75%+ coverage on a trigger and a controller
Read debug logs and set log levels in the Developer Console
Complete Org Development Model and Command-Line Interface; compare sandbox types and scratch orgs
Redo the practice questions and flashcards in all four Cert Prep modules
Take timed practice sets in this app and revisit your weakest section
Re-read the exam guide objectives and check you can explain each one
Book or confirm your exam and run the Pearson VUE system test

notes: Name: the exam guide and credential page call it 'Salesforce Certified Platform Developer'; 'Platform Developer I' survives only in URLs and older materials. The guide shows no exam code (older materials used Plat-Dev-201); not confirmed, so left out of the name.

Release: the exam guide (read 2026-11-16) says questions align to the Summer '25 release (API 64.0), while the current docs are Winter '27 (API 68.0). Apex classes saved at API 67.0+ run database operations in user mode and default to 'with sharing'; at API 66.0 and earlier, system mode is the default and an undeclared class usually runs without sharing. Question writers should follow the exam's release for these defaults or avoid questions that depend on them.

Agentforce for Developers: the developer.salesforce.com overview page now presents the tool as 'Agentforce Vibes'; the exam guide and Trailhead module still say 'Agentforce for Developers'. Keep exam wording, mention the new name once.
Unscored items: the guide says 'up to five'; 5 is the maximum, not a guaranteed count.

Delivery: Trailhead Academy booking and Pearson VUE delivery are confirmed by the Trailhead help article on online proctoring; the guide itself only says 'onsite at a testing center or in an online environment'.
Exam outline wording: the guide writes 'multi-tenant'; the Trailhead cert prep unit writes 'multitenant'. Objectives here are copied from the exam guide.
Pricing in other currencies beyond USD and JPY was not checked.

Governor limits: the current Execution Governors and Limits page (Winter '27) lists total heap as 10 MB sync / 25 MB async; older docs say 6 MB / 12 MB. Not confirmed which value applied at Summer '25, so avoid exam questions on the heap number.
